pro_course_detail.title: Standard Arabic
pro_course_detail.description:
Level 1: Basic Arabic (A1 & A2)
The elementary level is intended for students with little or no prior exposure to Arabic. Participants will learn to read and write using the Arabic alphabet and acquire the skills needed to conduct simple conversations concerning daily needs. Students begin building a vocabulary base and are introduced to basic grammar and syntax structures. By the end of level one, students should be able to satisfy routine social demands and limited work requirements.

Level 2: Intermediate Arabic (B1 & B2)
Students entering the intermediate level should be able to speak clearly, converse on limited subjects, and read and write simple texts. This level emphasizes techniques for reading, research and composition in Arabic, as well as advanced conversational skills. Audio-visual and published materials are introduced to reinforce listening and reading comprehension. Students gain increased confidence in grammar and syntax and concentrate on expanding their vocabulary base. At the end of this level, students should be able to speak, read and write confidently on various subjects, including: politics, religion, economics and culture.

Level 3: Advanced Arabic (C1 & C2)
Advanced participants should be able to speak confidently and clearly in most situations and be capable of reading and writing on different subjects with relative ease. The advanced level emphasizes overall reading comprehension, advanced writing skills, translation techniques and continued vocabulary acquisition. In addition to texts introduced for class work and home study, course material may also reflect the individual needs and interests of the advanced student. Participants who successfully complete this level should possess Arabic skills acceptable for academic or professional use.

pro_course_detail.description:
Do you want to sound better, and also improve your LISTENING comprehension dramatically? Well, the way you speak is the way you expect to hear. Better listening comprehension means you can enjoy learning using radio, TV and movies — enjoying all the benefits of authentic native-speaker material.

This course can be taken at any time, but it is most advantageous to do so before memorizing thousands of words with inaccurate pronunciation, and before spending countless hours practicing bad prosody in conversations.

No, you will not be able to pass for a native speaker after just one session :) The goal of this course will be to aim for near-native pronunciation while we make steady progress each lesson. Language coaching is provided so you can maximize your self-study outside of our sessions.

My philosophy: You do not need “accent reduction” — you do not need to reduce anything. Your native accent is perfect — for your native language. What you need is accent acquisition — to acquire a subconscious mastery of the characteristic phonology of your target language that will allow you to speak “naturally” and LISTEN as easily as a native.

Depending on your personal goals and what we uncover during our first conversation, we may perfect your consonants, vowels, stress, intonation, rhythm, etc. We can improve all of these at either a basic or advanced level, as needed.

Video or just audio — it’s your decision, as I can tell exactly how you’re using your lips, tongue, etc., just by listening.

The price of this course is a little bit higher than the standard “Conversational English with Integrated Grammar” because 99.9% of English teachers don’t have the skills to teach it. You will experience noticeable improvement after every session — guaranteed. Write me for additional information.

teacher_info.teaching_style:
My general teaching style is conversational, as I believe the best way to learn and develop skills is to find and pursue your own personal interests in the topic. You can learn (and more importantly, remember) far more from a conversation about life than from going through a verb conjugations test for the 50th time!

This said, I also absolutely love any opportunity to get into serious English grammar, and I am available to answer any question that a student might have about the language -- from word definitions and the differences between synonyms, to gerunds and adverbs. :)

exp_info.description: I taught as an Assistant English Teacher in a high school in El Escorial, near Madrid, Spain. It was valuable experience for teaching in a completely foreign environment, with a range of students, some with no English experience and some completely fluent.

I taught native English speakers who were having difficulty in middle/high school, due either to environmental challenges or to slight learning disabilities. It was a wonderful experience to learn how to teach kids from different angles, and see how with just the right application of teaching, they could thrive just as much as anyone else.
